metadata.title: Claude, Cash Flow Snapshot.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude wrote custom logic for the cash-flow-snapshot skill, using the skill's own documented mechanism as the case. Lands the carry-out that a skill is a pre-written file Claude reads and follows, not code Claude improvises, and that determinism (same input, same output) is both the guarantee and the limit.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (the 'cash flow snapshot - March' request, submitted, walked through the same three steps, run twice)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes Claude built the cash-flow-snapshot skill itself, writing the logic on the fly. It didn't. Claude reads a file someone else wrote and follows it, step by step. What's actually in that file?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Claude built the cash-flow-snapshot skill. Right?', hesitates on 'built', corrects to 'reads', lands the real question

props.text:
Claude built the
cash-flow-snapshot
skill.
Right?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('built' -> 'reads') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Open the cash-flow-snapshot folder and there's no hidden script waiting to run the real logic. Two items: a SKILL.md file — about six kilobytes of plain language — and a reference folder beside it. Claude reads that SKILL.md itself and treats it as the program. There's nothing else in there to find.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder listing opens to exactly two items — SKILL.md and reference/ — nothing else; the SKILL.md tile highlighted as the program itself

production_viz.label: No hidden script — two items, that's all
production_viz.mechanic: A folder icon opens onto exactly two tiles: SKILL.md (6k) and reference/. No third tile appears no matter how long the frame holds. The SKILL.md tile is outlined and a caption pins under it: 'this file IS the program.'

beats.narration_text: The pipeline lives in the Steps section, and Claude runs it top to bottom — linear, no branching unless a step says so. Ask it for a cash flow snapshot covering March, and it reads the SKILL.md, works through each step in order, and hands back a snapshot — the same steps, every single time.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — a 'cash flow snapshot · March' request goes in, three ordered steps light up in sequence, an output card comes out

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — request in, steps in order, output out
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A request card 'cash flow snapshot · March' enters from the left. Three numbered step tiles (STEP 1, STEP 2, STEP 3) light up left to right, one at a time, never out of order. An output card labelled 'SNAPSHOT — MARCH' appears on the right. THIS EXACT REQUEST AND STEP SEQUENCE RETURN AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Ask for that same March snapshot again, and the answer comes back identical — not because Claude re-examined the numbers with fresh judgment, but because the exact same steps ran a second time. That cuts both ways: identical output on identical input doesn't prove Claude understood anything about cash flow — it only proves the fixed steps repeated. And different output next month, on different numbers, doesn't mean the logic changed either — the same steps just ran on new input.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same March request submitted twice, two identical output cards; beside it, a different month's request producing a different card from the same three steps

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same input twice, then a different input
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 REQUEST RETURNS, identical, run through the same three step tiles again. Two 'SNAPSHOT — MARCH' output cards sit side by side, character-for-character identical. Beside them, a third run: 'cash flow snapshot · April' enters the same three steps and exits as a visibly different output card. A caption under all three: 'same steps, every time — the input is what changes.'

beats.narration_text: A Claude skill isn't code Claude writes on the fly. It's a file someone already wrote, that Claude reads and follows the same way, every single time.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Open the cash-flow-snapshot skill folder. Before you run anything, read me the SKILL.md and tell me, in your own words, what steps it says to follow, in order. Liam, in for Bear.
